# Create or Update Pull Request

Create or update a pull request for the current Git branch. If an argument is provided, use it as the base branch; otherwise default to `main`.

## Step-by-step workflow

### 1. Gather context

- Run `git remote get-url origin` to determine the GitHub owner and repo name.
- Run `git branch --show-current` to get the current branch name.
- Run `gt log --short` to check if the current branch is part of a Graphite stack.
- Run `git log <base>..<current-branch> --oneline` to list all commits on this branch.
- Run `git diff <base>..<current-branch> --stat` to get a summary of changed files.
- Run `git diff <base>..<current-branch>` to read the full diff of all changes.

### 2. Check for an existing PR

- Use the GitHub MCP tool `search_pull_requests` to look for an open PR from the current branch into the base branch.
- If a PR already exists, check its `state`. Only reuse it if the state is `open`. If the PR is `closed` or `merged`, ignore it and create a new one.
- If an open PR exists, note its number — you will update it instead of creating a new one.

### 3. Check for a PR template

- Look for a pull request template in the repo:
  - `.github/pull_request_template.md`
  - `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/` directory
  - `pull_request_template.md` in the repo root
- If a template exists, use its structure for the PR body.

### 4. Review and update the README

- Read the project's `README.md` (if one exists).
- Compare it against the actual changes in the branch. Check for:
  - New commands, features, or subcommands that aren't documented.
  - Removed features or options still referenced in the README.
  - Changed behavior (e.g. renamed flags, new environment variables, altered workflows).
  - Outdated descriptions of packaging, build steps, or project structure.
- If the README needs updates:
  - Edit the README to reflect the current state of the code.
  - Commit the README change on the current branch with a clear commit message like `Update README to reflect recent changes`.
  - Push the commit to the remote branch.
  - Include the README updates as a section in the PR description.
- If the README is already accurate, skip this step.

### 5. Push the branch

- First, check if Graphite is available and configured for this repo:
  - Run `gt log --short 2>/dev/null` — if it errors or the branch is untracked, Graphite is not set up.
  - If `gt log` works and the branch is tracked, try `gt submit --stack`. If it fails (e.g. repo not synced), fall back to `git push`.
- If Graphite is available and working:
  - Use `gt submit --stack` to push the branch and create/update the PR.
  - `gt submit` in non-interactive mode creates draft PRs. Always follow up with `gh pr ready <number>` to mark it ready for review.
- If Graphite is not available or fails:
  - Use `git push -u origin <branch>` to push the branch.
  - Create the PR using the GitHub MCP `create_pull_request` tool.

### 6. Write the PR title and description

- Write a concise, descriptive PR title summarizing the overall theme of the changes.
- Write a comprehensive PR body with:
  - **Summary** (bullet points)
  - **Usage** (code example if applicable)
  - **Changes** (per-file)
  - **Test plan** (checklist)
- Match the style of existing PRs in this repo.
- Use markdown formatting with headers, tables, and bullet points for readability.
- **Important**: When passing the `body` to the GitHub MCP `create_pull_request` or `update_pull_request` tools, use actual newlines in the string — NOT literal `\n` escape sequences. Literal `\n` will render as visible text in the PR description instead of line breaks.

### 7. Update the PR description

- `gh pr edit` errors on this repo (classic projects deprecation). Use the GitHub MCP tool `update_pull_request` to set the title and body instead.
- If the PR already existed, check if there are new commits since the PR was last updated and reflect those in the description.

### 8. Report the result

- Print the PR URL so the user can review it.
- Summarize what was done (created vs updated, README changes, etc.).

input.body:
## Summary

Local iMessage moves out of `@spectrum-ts/imessage` into a new, explicitly-installed `@spectrum-ts/imessage-local` package. The goal (ENG-1953) is to keep the native SQLite dependency out of cloud installs: local iMessage relies on `@photon-ai/imessage-kit`, which pulls in `better-sqlite3` (a native module). Cloud deployments that only use managed lines should never have to build or install it.

- **New `@spectrum-ts/imessage-local`** — a macOS-only provider that reads the local Messages database via `imessage-kit`. It is intentionally **not** part of the batteries-included `spectrum-ts` metapackage.
- **`@spectrum-ts/imessage` is now cloud-only** — the `imessage-kit`/`better-sqlite3` dependency and every `isLocal()` branch are gone.
- **`Spectrum({ platforms: [...] })`** is now the canonical registration key; **`providers` stays as a working compatibility alias**.
- Release guards + a boundary test enforce that the native SQLite dependency can never leak back into the cloud package.

## Motivation

`imessage-kit` → `better-sqlite3` is a native dependency that only the local Messages-database path needs. Bundling it into the batteries-included package forced every cloud deployment to install/compile it. Splitting local iMessage into its own package removes it from cloud dependency graphs entirely, while a release check fails the build if it ever reappears.

## Migration

`imessage.config({ local: true })` has been removed. Install the local package and import `imessage` from it:

```ts
// Before
import { Spectrum } from "spectrum-ts";
import { imessage } from "@spectrum-ts/imessage";

const app = await Spectrum({
  providers: [imessage.config({ local: true })],
});
```

```ts
// After
import { Spectrum } from "spectrum-ts";
import { imessage } from "@spectrum-ts/imessage-local"; // bun add @spectrum-ts/imessage-local

const app = await Spectrum({
  platforms: [imessage.config()],
});
```

The cloud import is unchanged (`@spectrum-ts/imessage` or `spectrum-ts/providers/imessage`). Do not register cloud and local iMessage in the same `Spectrum()` instance — both represent the `"iMessage"` platform.

## Changes

### New package — `packages/imessage-local`
- `src/index.ts`: a fresh `definePlatform("iMessage", …)` scoped to local capabilities. Send/receive text, attachments, and contacts; deterministic DM references via `space.create`/`space.get`; universal `app(...)` content degrades to its URL as text; typing is a no-op. Remote-only operations (reactions, replies, effects, `streamText`, rename, avatar, membership, `leaveSpace`, backgrounds, mini-app cards, contact-card sharing, `getAttachment`, `read`) throw `UnsupportedError`.
- `src/local/*` and `test/local/inbound.test.ts` moved here from `@spectrum-ts/imessage` (git renames). Shared `content/*` and `shared/*` helpers are consumed from the cloud package via relative imports, wired through `tsconfig.json` `include` and `turbo.json` `inputs`.
- Depends on `@photon-ai/imessage-kit` + `zod`; peer-deps `@spectrum-ts/core`. Adds `README.md`, `tsdown.config.ts`, `turbo.json`, `vitest.config.ts`, and `test/provider.test.ts`.

### Cloud provider — `packages/imessage`
- Dropped the `@photon-ai/imessage-kit` dependency and every `isLocal()` guard. `IMessageClient` is now just `RemoteClient[]`; `local` is removed from `configSchema`; `isLocal` deleted.
- Inlined the iMessage message-effect constant map (`messageEffects`) in `content/effect.ts` instead of importing `MessageEffect` from `@photon-ai/advanced-imessage` (same string values).
- Removed local-mode unit tests that no longer apply (contact-card, membership, read-actions, remote/app, remote/stream-text, space).

### Core — `packages/core`
- `Spectrum()` accepts `platforms` as the canonical option, with `providers` retained as a compat alias. Exactly one must be supplied (schema `.refine()` + typed overloads via `SpectrumFactoryOptions`/`PlatformSelection`). Install-hint text now says `Spectrum({ platforms: [...] })`.

### Release guards
- `scripts/release/check-artifacts.ts`: fails the release if the published cloud `@spectrum-ts/imessage` dist contains `@photon-ai/imessage-kit` or `better-sqlite3`.
- `packages/spectrum-ts/test/imessage-package-boundary.test.ts`: asserts local iMessage is absent from the batteries-included package, `imessage-kit` is absent from the cloud provider, and `imessage-kit` ships only with the local package.

### Docs
- Reworked the iMessage docs around the two-package model: cloud vs. local quick starts, a feature-comparison table, a `local: true` migration section, and troubleshooting entries (native SQLite in cloud builds, Full Disk Access, edge/runtime caveats).
- `providers` → `platforms` across the docs; tapback constants replaced with universal `Emoji.*` aliases.

## README updates

Per the create-PR review step, the package READMEs were reconciled with the code (committed on this branch):

- **`packages/spectrum-ts/README.md`** — the showcase imported `telegram` from the `imessage` path while calling `imessage.config()`; fixed the binding to `imessage` in both the metapackage and lean-install snippets.
- **Root `README.md`** — switched the example to the `platforms` key, added the **Local iMessage** row to the platform table, pointed the "connect to a local iMessage database" sentence at `@spectrum-ts/imessage-local`, and replaced "every official provider" / "all providers" with "the standard provider set".

## Breaking changes

- `imessage.config({ local: true })` is removed — use `@spectrum-ts/imessage-local`.
- The cloud `imessage` static effect map is now the local `messageEffects` constant (identical string values) rather than advanced-imessage's `MessageEffect`.
- Docs move iMessage reactions from `imessage.tapbacks.*` to universal `Emoji.*` aliases.
- `Spectrum({ providers: [...] })` still works — non-breaking compat alias.

## Test plan

- [ ] `bun install` (lockfile updated with the new package)
- [ ] `bun run typecheck`
- [ ] `@spectrum-ts/imessage-local` unit tests pass on Node and Bun (`test:node`, `test:bun`)
- [ ] `@spectrum-ts/imessage` unit tests pass after local-mode removal
- [ ] `@spectrum-ts/core` tests pass (`platforms`/`providers` option)
- [ ] `imessage-package-boundary` test passes
- [ ] Release artifact check rejects forbidden imports in the cloud dist
